rationale:
Evidence: all 60 trials of iterations 0-4 ended off track with exactly one line-loss event each. max_error sits at about 0.061 m, just over the fixed 0.06 m limit, in every design. Oval progress stayed near 0.11 across all five designs, so the failure is a shared early event, not a gain problem. Gains (kp 1.6 to 6, kd 0.05 to 0.3, ki 0 to 0.3) and speed (1.2 to 1.8) changed little. Sensor moves changed s-bend and slalom progress (0.04 to 0.15), so sensing geometry is the main lever. Most likely mechanism: the robot swings about 0.035 m off centre, the tape leaves the sensor array, the line is lost, and the 0.35 throttle recovery drifts it past 0.06 m. The array spans only +/-0.03 m, so it loses the tape too early.

Changes: (1) Widen the array to x = -0.06 to +0.06 m at 0.02 m spacing, 7 sensors, y = 0.08 m. The tape should stay visible through a larger swing, so the line-loss event should move later or disappear. (2) Keep the weights linear and antisymmetric, [-1.5, -1.0, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5]. The wider spacing halves the signal change per metre of offset, so kp rises from 1.6 to 2.5 to restore the same correction strength. (3) kd raised from 0.3 to 0.5 to damp the swing that drives the robot toward the loss threshold. (4) base_speed lowered from 1.2 to 1.1 to give the loop more time to correct on bends. The pace cost is small, since the average speed needed for finishing is about 1.5 m/s and the bends are the limit. (5) Mass lowered from 0.8 to 0.6 kg to reduce yaw inertia, so turns respond faster. wheel_track 0.14, wheel_radius 0.03, body unchanged, line_loss last_direction kept so this change isolates sensing and damping.

Expected result: fewer or later line-loss events, max_error below 0.06 m on at least the s-bend and slalom, and progress rising toward 0.3 or more on the oval. If line loss still happens at the same point, the next revision should test line_loss or the start handling rather than gains.
